description:
Workspace AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields' section gives this canonical example for forward-compatible result-enum shape:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum MailboxRole {
    Inbox,
    Sent,
    // ... known RFC 8621 §2.1.1 variants ...

    /// Forward-compat catch-all for vendor / site / future-spec roles.
    /// The wire string is preserved for round-trip.
    #[serde(other)]
    Unknown(String),
}
```

The policy text explicitly names `MailboxRole` and uses `Unknown(String)` as the catch-all variant. But the actual `MailboxRole` in crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs:43 declares `Other(String)`, and so does every sibling extension-types crate:

- jmap-mail-types: MailboxRole, Delivered, Displayed, UndoStatus, ComparatorProperty — all use Other(String)
- jmap-chat-types: presence.rs, message.rs (×2), chat.rs — all Other(String)
- jmap-calendars-types: notification.rs — Other(String)
- jmap-tasks-types: notification.rs, task_list.rs, task.rs — all Other(String)

This is a workspace-wide consistency gap between the policy doc and the actual canonical code. Two ways to resolve:

(A) Update the workspace AGENTS.md policy text to say `Other(String)` (matches all existing code; zero code churn; existing rustdoc that says 'Other' stays accurate). `#[serde(other)]` already works with any variant name — the attribute is what matters, not the variant identifier.

(B) Rename every existing `Other(String)` to `Unknown(String)` across all extension-types crates, plus update the impl_string_enum! macro in jmap-types to emit `Unknown` instead of `Other`. This is a public-API breaking change in 14+ crates touching ~10 enums each.

Recommendation: (A). The variant identifier is a Rust-side naming choice that the wire format doesn't see; `Other` is the de-facto pattern across the workspace; `Unknown` would force a downstream-breaking rename for no engineering benefit. The policy doc should match the code.

This is a workspace-wide decision (touches jmap-types macro definition and every extension-types crate). Filing as a human-decision bead.

Cross-reference: workspace AGENTS.md 'Extras-preservation policy for vendor/site fields'.
